label: copy-phase re-input of q/z before p/l/r (sparse, conjunctive)
explanation: Very sparse feature (~0.005% of steps), copy phase only; never fires in the original or delimiter phases, and only fires at repeated tokens (in_first=0). 75% of activation mass is at recall_idx 1, where the input is the just-copied first token, mostly q (51% of mass) or z (33%), with smaller amounts for 3 and f. It is concentrated in short sequences (L=3: 46% of mass, L=4: 27%) and near the end of the copy (to_go 1-2). The strongest activations (0.8-1.0 of max) are sequences like q p l <DEL> q, where the next output is p, l or r. But the feature is highly conjunctive and unreliable: copy-phase q/z input with to_go<=2 covers 74% of activations at 0.2% precision. Restricting to L=3, recall_idx 1, next output p/l/r reaches 53% precision but only 15% recall. No simple predicate gets F1 above about 0.23 on dev.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=q (+4.54), t=4 & prev_tok=<DEL> (+4.09), phase=2 & in_tok=z (+4.00), next_out=l (+2.62), next_out=p (+2.54), phase=2 & out_tok=p (+2.32). Lower it: prev2_tok=<DEL> (-2.14), in_first=1 (-2.07), prev3_tok=<DEL> (-1.78), to_go=4 (-1.59).
